sentences.text: The Corruption and Crime Commission assessed inherent corruption and misconduct risks across the WA public sector in 2014.
sentences.support: In 2014 the Commission conducted its inaugural misconduct intelligence assessment of the Western Australian public sector.

sentences.text: It collected and analysed information from about 300 government departments, local governments and other organisations, without assessing the adequacy of their existing controls.
sentences.support: it does not examine the adequacy of the control environment in place to mitigate those inherent risks.

sentences.text: The Commission identified high risks in corrective services, local government, procurement, regulation, transport, health and policing.
sentences.section: Use of Findings by the Commission
sentences.support: those public sector agencies and activities identified as high risk through the assessment process now regarded as priority areas

sentences.text: It used the assessment to set its priorities and urged agencies to incorporate their own risks into planning, governance and controls.
sentences.section: Use of Findings by the Public Sector
sentences.support: ensure they have appropriate control strategies and governance frameworks in place to adequately manage and mitigate them.

findings.quote: The changing nature and operating environment of the Western Australian public sector gives rise to new corruption threats and misconduct risks.

notes: No separate executive summary or overview. This assesses inherent risks, not actual misconduct or the effectiveness of agencies' controls. No numbered recommendations list.
